A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOBOLFI work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–D. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian/Brownian and MLBA simulations, analysis of Singapore drivers' choice and response-time data, and day-care infection simulations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised real-data posterior estimates and expanded discrepancy checks.

M1.justification: The real-data MLBA application changes the discrepancy objectives supplied to MOBOLFI: mean RT distance and a Brier-score choice discrepancy become log-transformed RT distance and choice-proportion SSE objectives (Equations 4.7–4.8). The general multivariate GP, NEHVI acquisition, and likelihood-approximation framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Gaussian/Brownian toy scenarios, synthetic MLBA, the Singapore survey with 149 participants and 584 observations, and the Appendix D day-care simulation. Revised empirical checks do not introduce a new population, domain, or task.

E2.justification: The empirical comparison against MOBOLFI using the single-simulation discrepancy design Δ is removed with v1 Figure 14. BOLFI, closed-form posterior benchmarks, and the synthetic MOBOLFI AUX comparison remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.3 changes empirical initialization from 100 prior draws to 282 space-filling points and simulator replicates from 30 to 50. It also changes discrepancy definitions and reports posterior means instead of MAP markers in Figure 5. These constitute a substantial revision of the real-data protocol.

E4.justification: The empirical appendix loses the fixed-versus-free λ2 analysis, the discrepancy-design ablation, and the parameter-sensitivity sweep. The MAP discrepancy check is revised and expanded to posterior means in v3 Figure 6, with additional point-estimate comparisons in Figure 15. Synthetic tolerance, acquisition-budget, and misspecification analyses remain.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Table 1 removes tabulated posterior standard deviations and 95% highest-density intervals for the MLBA variants. Posterior-density reporting remains, and discrepancy histograms retain 1000 replicates while expanding to additional point estimates.

E6.justification: The empirical posterior results in Figure 5 are replaced. Whereas v1 Appendix Figure 15 reports similar discrepancy distributions at MOBOLFI and closed-form MAPs, v3 Figure 6 shows larger discrepancies for MOBOLFI posterior means on both sources and a MAP tradeoff: smaller RT but larger choice discrepancies. These are results under revised settings, not direct performance changes under identical conditions. Empirical ablation and sensitivity results are also removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1, Equation C.2 replaces the normal density φ with the normal CDF Φ in the term multiplied by −(χ−tda)/A, correcting the accumulation-time CDF expression. Equations 4.7–4.8 also redefine the empirical discrepancy functions. The general GP derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The three stated MOBOLFI contributions and applicability beyond SSMs remain. However, the introduction narrows its contrast with earlier LFI: instead of saying BayesFlow and most LFI overlook relationships between sources, v3 acknowledges existing multi-source inference and emphasizes source-specific model checks rather than global adequacy checks.

C2.justification: The empirical interpretation shifts from weak discrepancy sensitivity to β and λ1 toward a choice-informed front-end versus RT-informed back-end explanation and posterior-mean/MAP fit tradeoffs. The justification for fixing λ2=0 changes from fitted model-variant evidence to a prospect-theory argument. The previous sensitivity-based explanation is removed with Appendix C.4.3.

D1.justification: The empirical implementation documentation specifies revised initialization, replication counts, and discrepancy normalizations. Removing Appendix C.4.3 also removes its parameter-grid and simulation instructions. Code-access information and most GP, MCMC, and synthetic-experiment details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially repositions the work around simulation-efficient inference and model misspecification rather than consumer-choice and attention research. It adds discussion citing Bahg et al. (2020), Frazier et al. (2020), Ward et al. (2022), and Wilkinson (2013), while removing several choice-process references and revising its characterization of earlier multi-source LFI.

P1.justification: The abstract opening and much of the introduction are substantially rewritten around generative statistical models. The empirical methods and interpretation are extensively revised, and Appendix C.4 changes from three detailed subsections to a short mean-versus-MAP discussion. These changes exceed routine language editing.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with reordered panels, revised axes, and mean markers replacing MAP markers. The two-panel appendix discrepancy histogram becomes an expanded four-panel main-text Figure 6. Table 1, the empirical discrepancy-ablation display, and sensitivity boxplots disappear; v3 adds a focused two-parameter point-estimate display. Other figures are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 improves statistical positioning, corrects the CDF expression, and makes empirical fit differences more transparent through Figure 6. However, it changes the empirical objectives and settings while removing model-selection evidence, discrepancy ablations, and sensitivity diagnostics. These gains in clarity and transparency coexist with reduced validation of the empirical application; the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
